claims.claim_text: Valuing consistency means judging hidden anchor processes, not surface behavior
claims.evidence_quote: What I'm actually trying to evaluate is the process: what the person's anchor is ... whether the movement ... came from evidence or from cost
claims.reasoning: Title plus summary compress the closing thesis with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: Consistency is vague yet morally loaded: compliment and accusation at once
claims.evidence_quote: vaguer than I'd like ... sometimes it's a compliment, sometimes an accusation
claims.reasoning: Vagueness plus dual moral valence match the opening.

claims.claim_text: Example: mini skirts to chador after 1979 versus steady modesty across the revolution
claims.evidence_quote: wore mini skirts all the time. Right after the revolution she switched to chador and niqab ... dressed modestly before ... and ... after
claims.reasoning: Swing and steady cases match; dropping niqab from the conjunction is harmless compression since switching to chador is stated.

claims.claim_text: Updating beliefs is a virtue, so the swing itself cannot carry the moral weight
claims.evidence_quote: being able to update your beliefs ... is a virtue ... the swing itself can't be what we're judging
claims.reasoning: Update-as-virtue plus swing-cannot-carry-weight match.

claims.claim_text: Openness scale -1 to 1; society at -0.5 and 0.5; modest woman at -0.1 and 0.1
claims.evidence_quote: from -1 (fully closed) to 1 (fully open) ... -0.5 in the closed state and 0.5 in the open ... -0.1 in the closed state and 0.1 in the open
claims.reasoning: All five figure assignments match exactly.

claims.claim_text: Behavior is w times Reference plus (1-w) times Anchor; modest anchor 0, w 0.2
claims.evidence_quote: Behavior = w x Reference + (1-w) x Anchor ... the anchor is a = 0 ... w = 0.2
claims.reasoning: Formula and solved values match.

claims.claim_text: Output moved (-0.1, 0.1) while the rule never did: fixed twenty percent concession
claims.evidence_quote: Her output moved: -0.1 then 0.1 ... Her rule never did: same anchor, same responsiveness
claims.reasoning: Moved-output versus fixed-rule contrast matches; twenty percent restates w=0.2.

claims.claim_text: Model is a linear combination; economists might call anchor endogenous, reference exogenous
claims.evidence_quote: the model here is the most simple model ... a linear convex combination ... economists perhaps would call the anchor an indogenous variable, and the reference an exogenous variable
claims.reasoning: PS2 content matches including the hedged perhaps.

claims.claim_text: Chameleon at 0.9 and -0.9 yields anchor 0, w 1.8: overshoot by eighty percent
claims.evidence_quote: at 0.9 when society is 0.5, and at -0.9 when society is -0.5 ... anchor comes out to 0 ... w comes out to 1.8 ... overshoot it by eighty percent
claims.reasoning: Behaviors, solved values, and eighty-percent wording all match.

claims.claim_text: Her rule is exactly as consistent as the modest woman's; only content differs
claims.evidence_quote: Her rule is exactly as consistent as the modest woman's ... The difference ... is what the rule says
claims.reasoning: Equal-consistency plus content-difference match.

claims.claim_text: Consistency splits three ways: output, policy (anchor plus responsiveness), anchor itself
claims.evidence_quote: Consistency of output ... Consistency of policy ... Consistency of anchor
claims.reasoning: All three layers with the policy gloss match.

claims.claim_text: Policy can hold while the anchor drifts invisibly; drift carries the moral weight
claims.evidence_quote: Policy can stay fixed while the anchor drifts underneath it, invisibly ... That drift is where the moral weight lives
claims.reasoning: Invisible drift plus moral-weight location match.

claims.claim_text: Contrarian at 0.2 and -0.2 yields anchor 0, w -0.4: same model, flipped sign
claims.evidence_quote: observed at 0.2 when the average is -0.5, and at -0.2 when the average is 0.5 ... anchor ... 0 ... responsiveness ... -0.4 ... sign flipped
claims.reasoning: Observations, solved values, and flipped-sign gloss match.

claims.claim_text: Contrarianism is dependency with a minus sign, tracking the reference closely
claims.evidence_quote: Contrarianism is dependency with a minus sign, not independence
claims.reasoning: Signature sentence reproduced with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: Spectrum: above 1 amplifier; 1 absolute conformist; 0 to 1 partial; 0 independent
claims.evidence_quote: above 1 Amplifier ... 1 Absolute conformist ... between 0 and 1 Partial conformist ... 0 Independent
claims.reasoning: Four table rows match with postures intact.

claims.claim_text: -1 to 0 partial contrarian; -1 absolute contrarian; below -1 overshooting rebel, perhaps
claims.evidence_quote: between -1 and 0 Partial contrarian ... -1 Absolute contrarian ... below -1 ... a contrarian who overshoots, an extremist rebel?
claims.reasoning: Remaining rows match; perhaps preserves the source question mark hedge.

claims.claim_text: High or low responsiveness is neutral until the reference kind is asked
claims.evidence_quote: High or low responsiveness is neither good nor bad until you ask what kind of reference is in play
claims.reasoning: Neutrality-until-reference-kind matches.

claims.claim_text: Normative references (fashion, approval) merit resistance; structural ones (budget, body) tracking
claims.evidence_quote: A normative reference (peer pressure, fashion, social approval) ... resist. A structural reference (a deadline, a budget, a body, a risk exposure) ... track
claims.reasoning: Both reference kinds with examples and verdicts match.

claims.claim_text: IMHO |w| should be generally small with an educated anchor; this world is less than ideal
claims.evidence_quote: in an ideal world, IMHO the |w| should be generally small, and everyone should have an educated Anchor ... this is not an ideal world
claims.reasoning: IMHO qualifier, small-|w|, educated anchor, and non-ideal caveat all preserved.

claims.claim_text: Equity rule 110 minus age: about 85% stocks at 25, about 50% at 60
claims.evidence_quote: equity allocation at roughly 110 minus your age: about 85% stocks at 25, about 50% at 60
claims.reasoning: Rule plus both allocations with about qualifiers match.

claims.claim_text: Staying 85% equities at 65 from lifelong aggression is refusal, not conviction
claims.evidence_quote: An investor who stays at 85% equities at 65 because I've always been aggressive isn't showing conviction. They're refusing
claims.reasoning: Age, allocation, motive quote, and refusal verdict match.

claims.claim_text: Same moving form, opposite verdicts: the verdict depends entirely on reference kind
claims.evidence_quote: look superficially alike ... Morally they are opposites ... The verdict depends entirely on which kind of reference
claims.reasoning: Same-form opposite-verdict structure with entirely qualifier matches.

claims.claim_text: Evidence versus cost crossed with anchor moved or held yields four cells
claims.evidence_quote: Cross those forces with whether the anchor actually moved and you get four cells
claims.reasoning: Two-by-two structure matches the table.

claims.claim_text: Rational revision (evidence, moved) is good; ossification (evidence, held) is stubbornness as principle
claims.evidence_quote: Rational revision: the good case ... Ossification ... stubbornness in the costume of principle
claims.reasoning: Both evidence-column cells with valences match.

claims.claim_text: Preference laundering dresses social proof as re-examined belief
claims.evidence_quote: Social proof gets laundered into belief that was never actually re-examined
claims.reasoning: Laundering mechanism matches.

claims.claim_text: Anchor held under cost change splits into revealed preference versus hysteresis
claims.evidence_quote: Anchor held ... behavior still needs sorting: Revealed preference ... Hysteresis
claims.reasoning: Split of the held-under-cost cell matches.

claims.claim_text: Revealed preference: behavior snaps to anchor once cost drops; swing was suppression
claims.evidence_quote: Behavior snaps to the anchor once the cost of expressing it drops ... The swing is what suppression looked like from outside
claims.reasoning: Snap-back plus suppression-reading match.

claims.claim_text: Hysteresis: behavior never snaps back; installed fear runs on its own
claims.evidence_quote: Behavior fails to snap back even after the cost is gone, because the fear got installed deeply enough to run on its own
claims.reasoning: Failed snap-back plus installed-fear mechanism match.

claims.claim_text: Anchor nearer or farther from reference deliberately unexplored for lack of examples
claims.evidence_quote: I deliberately haven't explored the cases where the anchor is closer or farther from the reference ... couldn't come up with meaningful examples
claims.reasoning: PS1 scope exclusion with reason matches.

claims.claim_text: Perspective gain: grasp of a static reference can move, then overturn again
claims.evidence_quote: your grasp of it moves from nothing to something ... a second pass at the very same unchanged reference can overturn it again. Call it perspective gain
claims.reasoning: Static-reference movement plus overturning matches the footnote.

claims.claim_text: Revision and laundering can reach an identical anchor; often indistinguishable even inside
claims.evidence_quote: can produce an identical new anchor ... From outside they are indistinguishable. Often from inside too
claims.reasoning: Identical destination plus outside-and-often-inside indistinguishability match.

claims.claim_text: Example: socialist at 20, still socialist at 40: revision and laundering share one trajectory
claims.evidence_quote: If you're not a socialist at 20 ... If you're still a socialist at 40 ... the same trajectory falls out of ... both processes
claims.reasoning: Ages and shared-trajectory claim match.

claims.claim_text: I used to be naive fits both; nothing about the shift reveals which occurred
claims.evidence_quote: I used to be naive ... Nothing about the shift itself tells you which one occurred
claims.reasoning: Retrospective-story ambiguity matches.

claims.claim_text: Confounded attribution: correct belief via unreliable process fails when cost opposes evidence
claims.evidence_quote: A person can land on the objectively correct new anchor for the wrong reason ... follows cost again and gets it wrong that time
claims.reasoning: Right-answer-wrong-process plus later-failure logic matches.

claims.claim_text: Misperceived reference corrupts everything downstream with no layer flawed
claims.evidence_quote: This is an error upstream of anchor, responsiveness, and policy entirely. It corrupts every downstream judgment without any of those three being flawed
claims.reasoning: Upstream error plus unflawed-layers consequence match.

claims.claim_text: Reference lag: diaspora freezes the origin norm at emigration; Quebec keeps dropped features
claims.evidence_quote: the origin country's norm at the moment their family left it, frozen the day they emigrated ... Quebec French keeps features that metropolitan French has dropped
claims.reasoning: Frozen-at-emigration plus Quebec illustration match.

claims.claim_text: Prior prediction under the old regime, with reasons, is the trustworthy test
claims.evidence_quote: what the person predicted, before the circumstance changed, that they would do once it did, and on what grounds
claims.reasoning: Advance prediction with reasons as the separator matches.

claims.claim_text: Understand-incentives-by-40 is falsifiable; more-to-protect is incentives as insight
claims.evidence_quote: I'll understand incentives better by 40 is a falsifiable claim ... I'll have more to protect by 40 is a claim about future incentives wearing the vocabulary of insight
claims.reasoning: Both example predictions with their readings match.

claims.claim_text: Without prior prediction the case is underdetermined; never default to flattering
claims.evidence_quote: the case is underdetermined. The default should not be to assume the more flattering interpretation
claims.reasoning: Underdetermination plus no-flattering-default match.

claims.claim_text: Behavioral consistency was a bad proxy; the trusted question is asked in advance
claims.evidence_quote: consistency of behavior was never the thing ... It was a proxy, and a bad one ... the only question I really trust is the one asked in advance
claims.reasoning: Bad-proxy verdict plus advance-question trust match.
